requirement: Review the repo.
how_to_verify: Read README.md; the repository held a single 11-byte README at commit 0cf74e6, recorded in the design notes.

requirement: Review the attached document or the link to the chat.
how_to_verify: docs/DESIGN_SOURCE.md records what was retrieved from the shared conversation and what it contains; every design section is traced on the requirements page.

requirement: Create a project that can think and reason on its own.
how_to_verify: Run python -m selflearn run, then read a topic page: candidates are generated, attacked, scored and ranked without input.

requirement: It is a free-thinking project.
how_to_verify: Open questions are derived from retrieved evidence and from vocabulary the brief did not contain; the manager then chooses what to work on next.
gap: The engine writes no free prose. 'Thinking' here is candidate generation, criticism and ranking over verified claims. No language model exists in any stage of the pipeline - not as an option, not behind a flag - and adding one is explicitly out of scope (docs/ROADMAP.md, Deliberately not planned).

requirement: It should work continuously and nonstop.
how_to_verify: The cycle is idempotent and resumable; the workflow triggers it on a schedule and can be dispatched by hand.

requirement: Research topics and build solutions to the toughest problems using publicly available data.
how_to_verify: Every registered source is a public API with an operator and a documentation link; the sources page shows the last-run status of each.

requirement: It should be a competition to generate the most robust strategies and ideas.
how_to_verify: Each question gets one candidate per persona, a rule-based critique, a weighted scorecard and a head-to-head round; see the Competition section of any topic page.

requirement: Create an expanding library of new trending topics.
how_to_verify: The library is append-only JSONL; new questions are derived from retrieved evidence and every topic record is versioned.
gap: New-question generation is implemented; automatic seed-topic creation from live trend feeds is planned (the scoring function is written and the attention signal is measured, but no crawler adds topics on its own yet).

requirement: Become an expert at them by doing proper research.
how_to_verify: Each question accumulates claims, sources, contradictions, experiments and meta-knowledge about which sources are reliable.
gap: Depth is bounded by the budget per cycle and by which sources are reachable; a question only becomes 'validated' when supported claims, a surviving candidate and a test all exist.

requirement: Think through new ideas, implementing working line by line to build an easy to read summary.
how_to_verify: Every topic page has a generated Summary section whose figures are all engine-computed, followed by the exact statements and links behind them.
gap: Ingestion, identity resolution and the content store shipped on 2026-09-21 (evidence snapshots, stable ids, 14 JSONL streams) and the storage mirror with its reader shipped on 2026-09-22 (python3 -m selflearn storage sync/verify, Library.from_rows). Not implemented: MongoDB, Neo4j and Redis from the design document's reference stack; the graph database remains unused by choice (docs/LIMITATIONS.md item 23).

requirement: Self-free-thinking, expansive, continuously working and searching, researching new ideas.
how_to_verify: The loop searches, verifies, competes and derives new questions each cycle without input.
gap: Continuous operation needs a scheduler (provided) and, for the fullest form, credentials for the keyed sources. The engine reports every unreached source instead of pretending.

requirement: Learn from previous ideas.
how_to_verify: Every record is append-only with history; the meta-knowledge layer computes per-source support rates and per-rule survival rates from past cycles.

requirement: Work line by line verifying from official verified trusted sources, provide links for manual review.
how_to_verify: Every fact on the site shows the source link and the stored snapshot it was checked against; the review page lists everything the engine could not reconcile.

requirement: There should be no manual input; work on your own to complete tasks.
how_to_verify: A scheduled workflow runs the cycle end to end, commits the library and publishes the site. No command excludes a human, but none requires one.

requirement: Flag any irregularities for review.
how_to_verify: The audit stage produces classified findings with a suggested action for each; the review page renders them and reports.count is published.

requirement: No hallucinations.
how_to_verify: A claim is rejected if any number or date in it is absent from the cited document, or if polarity differs from the closest matching passage. The method page states the check and its thresholds.

requirement: Verify no hallucinations.
how_to_verify: The audit command re-derives every published claim from the stored byte-for-byte snapshot and reports any verdict that changed.

requirement: Get a full list that follows our requirements.
how_to_verify: Every line of the brief and every section of the design document appears in the matrix with a status and a verification method.

requirement: Create a GitHub page for this repo with clean UI, user friendly, simple and easy to use.
how_to_verify: The site is static, has no third-party requests, works without JavaScript, and is generated by python -m selflearn site.

requirement: It should be organized and clean.
how_to_verify: Seven pages with a fixed navigation, one stylesheet and a machine-readable JSON copy of every page under docs/data/.

requirement: Include all relevant information in an easy to read format with official verified links as sources for review.
how_to_verify: Facts are listed with their evidence class, verification score, confidence, quote, source link and stored hash.

requirement: Create a pull request and then merge it onto main.
how_to_verify: See the pull request referenced in the repository's merge commit and the closing summary.

requirement: Make suggestions for what work still needs to be done and limitations in the way of a successful project.
how_to_verify: The roadmap lists the next work in priority order; every limitation is stated on the overview and method pages.

requirement: Run this task through multiple passes (implement, review, re-check).
how_to_verify: docs/PASSES.md records what each pass found and changed, including the bugs fixed in pass two.

requirement: A world scanner that monitors papers, repositories, government datasets, filings, patents and feeds, and asks what changed.
how_to_verify: The register holds 36 machine-readable sources. Five of them publish a documented change filter (Crossref from-index-date, arXiv sortBy=submittedDate, GitHub pushed:>=, NVD lastModStartDate/lastModEndDate, USGS starttime/endtime) and selflearn/fetch/changes.py polls only those, recording the window used. Run 'python3 -m selflearn scan --offline' to see the five mechanisms, their endpoints and the operator documentation URL for each; the parameter names are pinned by tests/test_layers.py::ChangeScanTests.
gap: The remaining registered sources publish no documented change filter and are polled question by question; they are reported as having no change filter rather than as unchanged.

requirement: Topic intelligence: each topic gets an evolving record with facts, open questions, competing theories, evidence and experiments.
how_to_verify: Each topic page shows facts with verdicts, open questions with priorities, candidates with scorecards, contradictions and experiments.

requirement: Multiple independent thinkers with different briefs (conventional, contrarian, first principles, cross-domain, optimisation, experimental).
how_to_verify: The six briefs are defined with distinct claim-selection rules, so they genuinely look at different evidence.

requirement: The critic is as important as the researcher: attack every proposal, destroy bad ideas.
how_to_verify: Eleven named rules fire deterministically; each attack records the rule, the claims it looked at and a severity. An unresolved fatal attack vetoes a winner.

requirement: An explicit evidence hierarchy from direct experiment down to AI speculation, with provenance on every claim.
how_to_verify: Nine ranked classes; every claim stores the class and rank of the document it came from, and classes 6-9 can never ground a fact.

requirement: Structured memory in layers - raw evidence, knowledge, reasoning, experiments, meta-knowledge - rather than rewriting memory.
how_to_verify: Five append-only JSONL streams plus the snapshot directory; loading deduplicates by primary key with last-write-wins while the history stays on disk.

requirement: Every idea gets a lifecycle, and rejected ideas stay in the library.
how_to_verify: Nine lifecycle states; the stage is derived from the evidence held, never asserted, and nothing is deleted.

requirement: Automatic experimentation: build something, run it, compare to a baseline, keep the result.
how_to_verify: Experiments run in a subprocess with a timeout, a seed, a script hash and a captured result, and their output becomes rank-1 evidence.
gap: The catalogue is computational. Experiments that would need physical measurement cannot be run here; the engine records the gap rather than substituting a proxy.

requirement: Benchmark everything and select ideas Darwinianly.
how_to_verify: Each candidate is scored on nine criteria, with the method (measured or heuristic) published per criterion.
gap: A true benchmark per question requires a dataset and a metric per question. The engine has one for computational questions; for others the performance criterion stays at zero and says so.

requirement: A research tournament with rounds and a final, ranked on correctness, reproducibility, evidence quality, robustness and cost rather than rhetoric.
how_to_verify: Round-robin then final, with Elo accumulated across cycles; the criterion table and the veto rules are published on the method page.

requirement: The system needs curiosity: after finishing a question, ask what the result suggests next.
how_to_verify: Questions are derived from hedged findings, missing reference periods, transfers from other topics and new vocabulary; each records the claims it came from.

requirement: Trending-topic discovery: scan, detect emerging topics, score novelty, importance and research potential, select projects.
how_to_verify: selflearn/think/invention.py scores candidates as novelty x importance x potential with three gates (>=2 documents, novelty >= 0.5, total >= 0.45, at most 3 promotions per cycle). Every candidate, accepted or rejected, is published on the index page with its components and the reason. tests/test_layers.py::InventionTests covers the gates and the scaffolding regression.
gap: The candidate pool is the documents this engine has retrieved, not an open scan of the web, so 'novel' means novel to this library. That narrowing is published wherever a proposal appears.

requirement: A central research manager deciding what to research next and which hypotheses need testing.
how_to_verify: The manager scores questions, commits a task list to the library, chooses the reading list per question and enforces the request and document budget.

requirement: The final output must be extremely readable rather than a dump of agent conversations.
how_to_verify: Pages are short and structured: summary, unknowns, facts table, competition, experiments, questions, documents, status, and a manual check list.

requirement: A technology stack built from freely available components.
how_to_verify: The engine uses only the Python standard library, so it installs with no dependency resolution at all.
gap: The design document proposed PostgreSQL, a vector store, Neo4j and Redis/Celery. The engine still runs on JSONL plus files by default; the migration path the roadmap called for now exists end to end: 'python3 -m selflearn storage sync|verify' mirrors every stream into SQLite (standard library) or PostgreSQL (optional psycopg driver) and proves the two views identical row for row, 'site --from-database' and 'run --from-database' build the published site from that mirror and refuse to publish unless the views agree, and the TF-IDF vector index ('python3 -m selflearn retrieve') ranks cross-domain claim transfer. Not yet done: verifying the mirror against a live PostgreSQL server (none exists in this build environment and none can be installed here). Graph database, Redis and sandboxes remain deliberately unused.

requirement: Event-driven operation rather than one process thinking nonstop.
how_to_verify: One bounded cycle per invocation with hard budgets; the scheduler and the task queue in the library decide what runs next.

requirement: The core database structure: topics, questions, sources, claims, hypotheses, arguments, experiments, results, solutions, agents, projects, tasks, discoveries, failures, relationships, benchmarks.
how_to_verify: grep -n 'to_dict' selflearn/models.py selflearn/learn/store.py (every record type defines to_dict; store.py lists the streams and keys) - then python3 -m selflearn storage verify, which rebuilds a second view of the library from database rows through Library.from_rows and reports rows_identical: true, library_identical: true with matches: true on every stream

requirement: The system should be able to say UNKNOWN rather than forcing an answer.
how_to_verify: Every topic page has a 'What we do not know' section; a brief with no usable evidence declares itself blocked instead of guessing.

requirement: Recognise its own knowledge gaps: what we know, what we think we know, what we assume, what we do not know, what would change the conclusion, what experiment would resolve it.
how_to_verify: The six questions are rendered on every topic page; assumptions are listed per candidate and each candidate carries an explicit falsifier.

requirement: The ultimate architecture: scanner, knowledge base, question generator, research manager, competing researchers, critic, experiment engine, evaluator, reproduction, discovery engine, loop.
how_to_verify: Each box of the diagram maps to a module named in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, and the cycle executes them in that order.

requirement: No manual input: the engine runs and publishes on its own.
how_to_verify: The schedule starts a cycle every six hours, runs the tests, probes the sources, audits the library, exports the summary, commits the updated library and pages, and uploads the artefacts. A run into a temporary root is exercised on every push, which is what `SELFLEARN_ROOT` exists for.
gap: GitHub delays scheduled runs under load, so the interval is a target rather than a guarantee.

requirement: Give a reviewer the means to re-check a claim, an experiment and a figure by hand.
how_to_verify: `python3 tools/check_claim.py` prints a claim, its stored document, its hash, a fresh re-check and the link to open. `python3 tools/reproduce_experiment.py <id>` repeats a stored experiment and compares the result field by field, ignoring wall-clock fields explicitly.

requirement: Provide links to official, verifiable sources for manual review.
how_to_verify: All 36 registered sources carry their operator and the operator's own documentation URL; the four least certain links were re-checked against the live web and corrected, and the corrections are listed in the sources document. Every claim links to the document it was cut from. The GitHub Pages entry point at the repository root is generated from the same data as the site, so the published URL cannot drift from the pages it links to.
gap: Four sources need credentials and are registered but never polled in this environment.

requirement: Repair the PatentsView adapter against official sources, and close the flag with a note rather than deleting it.
how_to_verify: The register now points at https://api.uspto.gov/api/v1 with key USPTO_ODP_API_KEY. UsptoOdpSource issues GET /patent/applications/search?q=...&limit=N and GET /datasets/products/search?productTitle=..., both with the X-API-KEY header. The bulk-products response is parsed with the field names the operator publishes; any other shape is stored verbatim. Run: python3 -m unittest tests.test_layers.UsptoOdpAdapterTests -v. The migration facts and their official URLs are listed in docs/SOURCES.md item 1 under 'Flagged for review'.
gap: No live call has been made: no ODP key is configured in this repository, so the adapter is proven against the operator's documented shapes, not against a real response.

requirement: A substance filter so quantified claims lead and metadata is labelled honestly.
how_to_verify: Eight features with published weights summing to 1 (quantity, date, comparison, mechanism, caveat, specificity, verification, evidence) produce a score and one of three labels. Topic pages order claims by it and show the label in the facts table; the index page reports the library-wide split; the method page prints the rule. Run: python3 -m unittest tests.test_layers.SubstanceRuleTests -v, which includes the test that an unsupported claim can never outrank an equivalent supported one.
gap: The rule is lexical. Dense prose without a digit scores as metadata, and a claim reciting a number scores as substantive. It orders reading and labels; it never overrides a verification verdict.

requirement: Cross-document synthesis using the existing derived-claim machinery, with the same discipline.
how_to_verify: claim_kind='synthesis' statements cite the direct claims they were built from, may contain only figures present in those claims plus the recorded document and source counts, and are rejected outright if verify_synthesis does not support them. The audit recomputes each one from its citations and raises an error if a cited claim has gone or the recomputation disagrees. Run: python3 -m unittest tests.test_layers.SynthesisTests -v; the test_a_figure_absent_from_the_citations_is_rejected case proves an invented average is refused.
gap: Units are matched by the word that followed the number, so two sources using one word for different measures could be combined; those statements are published as needing review and no averaging is ever performed.

requirement: Change-driven scanning using only filters the operators document.
how_to_verify: Five mechanisms, each with the operator's documentation URL published beside it. 'python3 -m selflearn scan' reports the window, the request, the items returned and the items not seen before; '--discover' turns new items into questions; the scheduled workflow runs it every cycle. Run: python3 -m unittest tests.test_layers.ChangeScanTests -v to see every parameter name pinned to its documented form.
gap: Not yet observed against live sources from this repository: the sandbox used for this build reaches only the GitHub hosts. Items published in a window the engine could not reach appear as new on a later run, attributed to the wrong window.

requirement: Topic invention from a scan, with published score components and provenance.
how_to_verify: Candidates are phrases recurring in at least two retrieved documents' own prose, scored as novelty x importance x potential, gated on >=2 documents, novelty >= 0.5 and total >= 0.45, at most three promotions per cycle. Accepted and rejected candidates are both published with their components. Run: python3 -m unittest tests.test_layers.InventionTests -v, including the regression test that the engine's own scaffolding never becomes a candidate.
gap: The candidate pool is the engine's own retrieval, not an open crawl of the web, so 'novel' means novel to this library. Seed topics remain human-authored.

requirement: Verify links line by line from official sources and publish them for manual review.
how_to_verify: tools/verify_links.py resolves every URL in the register, the change mechanisms and the repository prose, and writes reports/link_check.json with the status, the URL after redirects and the error for each. The CI workflow runs it on GitHub's runners, where egress is unrestricted, and prints a summary. From a sandbox with limited egress the report records 'unreachable' with the transport error, which is distinguishable from a 404.
gap: The tool proves a link resolves and where it lands; it does not assert anything about the page's content. Content-level verification of the operator statements used in this session is recorded by hand in docs/SOURCES.md with the date.

requirement: Flag irregularities for review, and let a reviewer close one without destroying the record.
how_to_verify: Every finding is written to library/irregularities.jsonl and rendered on the review page. 'python3 tools/reject_topic.py --id <topic_id> --reason ...' appends a rejected record for the same primary key with a timestamp, a reason and an optional link, and records an info irregularity that a reviewer acted; the original record stays in the stream. 'python3 tools/resolve_finding.py --id <irr-... or con-...> --reason ... [--link URL]' does the same for an irregularity or a contradiction: a new row for the same key carrying resolution, resolved_at and resolution_link, with the original summary, detail and claim ids unchanged. The store carries a reviewer's decision forward when a later cycle re-detects the same finding, and '--reopen' reverses it explicitly. The review page shows open findings and, in a separate 'Resolved by a reviewer' table, the original text beside the reason. Run: python3 -m unittest tests.test_layers.ReviewerResolutionTests -v.
gap: Resolution is a repository operation (a commit), not a web form; there is no authentication or reviewer identity beyond the git history of the appended row.
